title: AOM semantic schema
supported_claim: Presentation form, bulk consistency, moisture condition, process, composition state, component-retention state, and chemical constituent are independent governed relations.
limitation: Schema remains subject to review and downstream compatibility planning.

title: ADR 0048 chemical identity composition and component model
supported_claim: Chemical identity, measured composition, material component, and product use remain independent; Cohort E owns whole-milk, native-fat, form, and held constituent cases.
limitation: Accepted architecture does not decide Cohort E row dispositions.

title: FoodOn facets
supported_claim: Food description combines independent facets and relations rather than forcing source, process, physical quality, and composition into one hierarchy.
limitation: FoodOn includes human-food and inherited LanguaL scope and is not a feed-regulatory catalogue.

title: Food physical quality facet
supported_claim: Physical quality distinguishes liquid, semiliquid, semisolid, and solid qualities while shape and form remain separate refinements.
limitation: FoodOn terms require concept-level mapping review before exact AOM alignment.

title: FoodOn structure and design
supported_claim: Observable qualities and transformation processes occupy separate branches and are linked to food objects by relations.
limitation: Architecture guidance does not define feed-industry labels or thresholds.

title: Food chemical component facet
supported_claim: Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, minerals, and related components are reusable chemical-component identities independent of measured amount.
limitation: FoodOn component hierarchy does not by itself establish exact ChEBI equivalence.

title: Carbohydrate CHEBI 16646
supported_claim: Carbohydrate has a governed chemical-entity identity suitable for concept-level mapping.
limitation: Broad class does not identify measured carbohydrate content or feed-material use.

title: Protein CHEBI 36080
supported_claim: Protein has a governed chemical-entity identity suitable for concept-level mapping.
limitation: Broad class does not identify measured protein content or feed-material use.

title: Starch CHEBI 28017
supported_claim: Starch has a governed chemical identity distinct from starch concentration and starch feed-material products.
limitation: Exact AOM mapping still requires label-collision and scope review.

title: Essential oil CHEBI 83630
supported_claim: Essential oil is represented as a chemical mixture and can serve as a constituent identity.
limitation: Mixture identity does not establish regulatory additive or feed-material use.

title: Lipid CHEBI 18059
supported_claim: Lipid supplies a broad external mapping candidate for fat and oil constituent categories.
limitation: Fat and oil are context-sensitive mixture categories and should not receive exact lipid equivalence without narrower review.

title: Quality assurance for animal feed analysis laboratories
supported_claim: Ash is residue remaining after controlled incineration and is an analytical result rather than one chemical constituent.
limitation: Method definition does not identify each mineral species in residue.

title: Feedipedia glossary
supported_claim: Ash approximates mineral matter after incineration and dried describes moisture removal rather than particle form.
limitation: Glossary definitions remain broad and material-specific evidence is still required.

title: Experiences with urea-molasses multinutrient blocks
supported_claim: A coherent block is a physical presentation that animals may consume by licking; block form and lick delivery are related but not synonymous.
limitation: Publication concerns multinutrient blocks and does not define every mineral formulation.

title: Urea-molasses multinutrient blocks
supported_claim: Feed blocks are solid multi-component formulations intended for gradual consumption.
limitation: Specific composition and regulatory status vary by formulation and jurisdiction.

title: Poultry offal meal
supported_claim: The mapped material is explicitly poultry offal meal and carries dried-meal composition data.
limitation: Nutrient-table page relies on linked family description for general production details.

title: Poultry by-product meal
supported_claim: Poultry offal meal belongs to animal by-products and poultry slaughter by-products that are rendered, ground, and dried.
limitation: Family-level process description should not be inherited automatically without confirming mapped-page scope.

title: Catalogue of feed materials consolidated text
supported_claim: Feed-material names and processing qualifiers distinguish product identity from analytical composition and presentation.
limitation: EU legal categories do not define universal ontology hierarchy outside regulatory scope.
